title: Canonical shifts and action units of the derived pullback tensor comparison
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with sheaves of commutative rings and a ring map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and the canonical derived pullback $L=Lf^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Give $L$ its canonical comparisons obtained by shifting flat-term K-flat resolutions, and derived tensor the localized signed comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated, lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. Let $\mu_{M,N}:L(M\otimes^L_{R_Y}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}LM\otimes^L_{R_X}LN$ be the canonical bifunctorial comparison of Stacks Tag 07A4 (an isomorphism of the kind asserted in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]), normalized on representatives as follows. Write $f^*$ for termwise module pullback, $e_P:L(QP)\cong Q(f^*P)$ for the computation isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and $r_{P,Q}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\cong QP\otimes^LQQ$ for the representative isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For K-flat complexes $P,Q$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and $V=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{R_Y}Q)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], $\mu_{QP,QQ}=(e_P^{-1}\otimes e_Q^{-1})\,r_{f^*P,f^*Q}\,Q(c_{P,Q})\,e_V\,L(r_{P,Q}^{-1})$, where $c_{P,Q}:f^*\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(f^*P\otimes f^*Q)$, $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, is the cochain comparison of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]; $\mu$ is the unique natural transformation with these components. Put $\Phi(M,N)=L(M\otimes^LN)$ and $\Psi(M,N)=LM\otimes^LLN$. For $i=1,2$, let $s^i_{\Phi,n}$ and $s^i_{\Psi,n}$ be the composite shift comparisons on these functors when their $i$th input is shifted by $n\in\mathbf Z$ (using the comparison for $L$ also on the shifted tensor input in $\Psi$). Then, with $U_1=(M[n],N)$ and $U_2=(M,N[n])$,
$$s^i_{\Psi,n}\circ\mu_{U_i}=\mu_{M,N}[n]\circ s^i_{\Phi,n}.$$
There is a canonical isomorphism $u:L(R_Y[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X[0]$, obtained by pulling back the degree-zero ring complex. Write $\rho_M:M\otimes^LR[0]\cong M$ and $\ell_N:R[0]\otimes^LN\cong N$ (over $R=R_Y$ or $R_X$) for the right and left tensor action unitors: the unique natural isomorphisms whose components at $QP$, for $P$ flat-term K-flat, are the localizations of the chain maps $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes R[0])\to P$, $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$, and $\operatorname{Tot}(R[0]\otimes P)\to P$, $r\otimes y\mapsto ry$, composed with $r^{-1}$. For all $M,N$,
$$\rho_{LM}\circ(1\otimes u)\circ\mu_{M,R_Y[0]}=L(\rho_M),\qquad \ell_{LN}\circ(u\otimes1)\circ\mu_{R_Y[0],N}=L(\ell_N).$$
The shifts satisfy their zero and addition laws; the displayed equations are natural in both inputs, including all maps after localization. No flatness of the structural ring map, boundedness, direct image, adjunction, or projection mate is assumed in this statement.

proof.text: Write $A=R_Y$, $B=R_X$, $F=f^*$ termwise, and $Q_A,Q_B$ for localization. Let $\mathcal P_A$ be the flat-term K-flat complexes. The tensor-descent statement identifies their localization with $D(A)$ and makes restriction along $Q_A|_{\mathcal P_A}\times Q_A|_{\mathcal P_A}$ fully faithful on bifunctors. Thus equations between natural transformations can be tested on these representatives. For $P\in\mathcal P_A$ write $e_P:L(Q_AP)\cong Q_B(FP)$ for the canonical derived-pullback computation. It is natural in representative maps and compatible with their inversion. Shifts remain in $\mathcal P_A$. The canonical comparison $t_{P,n}:F(P[n])\cong(FP)[n]$ is termwise the identity: both differentials are $(-1)^nF(d_P)$. Consequently its localization, conjugated by $e_{P[n]}$ and $e_P[n]$, is precisely the stipulated comparison for $L$.

source.place: Tags 06YU (definition-derived-tor), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); shifting the chosen K-flat representatives

proof.text: For $P,Q\in\mathcal P_A$ put $V=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_AQ)$. The total-tensor-model lemma makes $V$ a flat-term K-flat representative of $Q_AP\otimes_A^LQ_AQ$. The derived tensor-pullback statement makes $FP,FQ$ flat-term K-flat as well. The statement prescribes the components $\mu_{Q_AP,Q_AQ}=(e_P^{-1}\otimes e_Q^{-1})\,r_{FP,FQ}\,Q_B(c_{P,Q})\,e_V\,L(r_{P,Q}^{-1})$, which is the construction in Tag 07A4 (there the inverse of $c$ is displayed). Each factor is an isomorphism ($r_{FP,FQ}$ exists because $FP,FQ\in\mathcal P_B$) and natural in homotopy maps of $P,Q$: $c$ by the cochain-coherence statement, $e$ by the pullback statement, $r$ by tensor descent, and $e_V$ for $\operatorname{Tot}$ of the maps, which preserves $\mathcal P_A$ by the total-tensor-model lemma. By the extension clause of tensor descent these components extend uniquely to a natural transformation of bifunctors $\Phi\to\Psi$; it is an isomorphism because every pair of objects is isomorphic to a pair $(Q_AP,Q_AQ)$, at which the component is invertible. The same extension clause, applied to the chain unitors (natural isomorphisms of complexes preserving $\mathcal P$, since $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes A[0])\cong P$), gives the action unitors $\rho,\ell$ of the statement. Its local formula is $b\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. All the inserted isomorphisms are natural, so this also specifies the normalization for shifted representatives.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), proof: the isomorphism of total complexes; inverse orientation to the displayed map there

proof.text:
First shift the first input. On representatives the desired square is
$$s^1_{B,n}\,(t_{P,n}\otimes1)\,c_{P[n],Q}=c_{P,Q}[n]\,t_{V,n}\,F(s^1_{A,n}).$$
Here $s^1_{A,n},s^1_{B,n}$ are the unsigned first-input total-tensor comparisons, and the notation on the left includes totalization of $t_{P,n}\otimes1$. On the summand with $x\in P^{p+n}$ and $y\in Q^q$, either composite sends $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, in the corresponding shifted summand. The maps $t$ are identities on coefficients and the maps $s^1$ introduce no sign. The cochain comparison and the shift maps are already chain maps by the cited statements. Equality on these local tensors is equality on each sheaf tensor summand and hence on the direct sum. This proves the first square before localization.

source.place: Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor), first input; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4, normalized cochain formula

proof.text:
For the second input the representative square is
$$s^2_{B,n}\,(1\otimes t_{Q,n})\,c_{P,Q[n]}=c_{P,Q}[n]\,t_{V,n}\,F(s^2_{A,n}).$$
On a summand $x\in P^p$, $y\in Q^{q+n}$, the left side is $(-1)^{np}(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. On the right, $F(s^2_{A,n})$ first contributes the same $(-1)^{np}$, since additive scalar extension sends multiplication by $-1$ to multiplication by $-1$; $c$ then gives the displayed tensor. Pullback changes neither degree $p$ nor $n$. Thus the two maps agree on every summand, as sheaf maps, and therefore as chain maps. This works for every integer $n$, including negative $n$, with no flatness condition on $f^{-1}A\to B$.

The comparisons $t_{P,0}$ are identities and $t_{P,n+m}$ is the composite of $t_{P[n],m}$ and $t_{P,n}[m]$, after the canonical shift-addition identification: each has identity components and differential $(-1)^{n+m}F(d_P)$. The total-tensor comparisons have their zero and addition laws by the integer-shift statement, and their localized comparisons are the ones specified by the fixed-tensor statement. For clarity, in the second input two successive shifts contribute $(-1)^{np}(-1)^{mp}=(-1)^{(n+m)p}$, while in the first input all components are unsigned. Hence the composite comparisons for $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ have these laws on representatives. Inserting the natural computation isomorphisms $e$ only conjugates these equations, so it preserves them.

source.place: Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor), zero and addition coherence of the separate input shifts

proof.text: The ring complex $A[0]$ is flat-term K-flat: tensoring by $A$ is the identity on module sheaves and hence exact, and total tensoring any acyclic complex by $A[0]$ is that same complex, with the same differential. These assertions use exactly the definitions of flatness, K-flatness and total tensor. Its termwise pullback is canonically $B[0]$: if $a\in f^{-1}A$, the map $j:F(A[0])\to B[0]$ is $b\otimes a\mapsto b\,c(a)$, with inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, where $c:f^{-1}A\to B$ is the structural ring map. The balanced tensor relations give both inverse identities. Therefore $u$ is $L(A[0])\xrightarrow{e_{A[0]}}Q_BF(A[0])\xrightarrow{Q_Bj}B[0]$. This construction uses $A[0]$ itself as the resolution, so requires no flatness of $c$.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), computation on the ring complex; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL, scalar-extension unit

proof.text:
For a flat-term K-flat $P$, evaluate the right-unit composite on $b\otimes(x\otimes a)$, with $a\in f^{-1}A$ in degree zero. The cochain comparison, followed by $1\otimes j$ and the right action, gives
$$b\otimes(x\otimes a)\longmapsto(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes a)\longmapsto(b\otimes x)\otimes c(a)\longmapsto b\,c(a)\otimes x=b\otimes ax.$$
This is $F(\rho_P)$. For the left-unit composite on $b\otimes(a\otimes y)$ the images are $(b\otimes a)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, then $b\,c(a)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, then $b\,c(a)\otimes y=b\otimes ay$, which is $F(\ell_P)$. These are also exactly the action-unitor compatibility asserted by the cochain-coherence statement. The ring factor has degree zero, so no Koszul sign occurs. Applying $Q_B$ and the natural $e$ comparisons from step 2 gives both required unit identities on representatives with the specific $u$ of step 6.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), cochain comparison; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL, scalar multiplication and action units

proof.text: The representative shift squares in steps 3 and 4, after the computation identifications in steps 1 and 2, are exactly $s^i_{\Psi,n}\mu_{U_i}=\mu_{M,N}[n]s^i_{\Phi,n}$ restricted to $(M,N)=(Q_AP,Q_AQ)$. All their arrows are natural there: $c$ is natural in complex maps, $e$ in resolution maps, and the tensor shift comparisons in each argument; the cited descent statements give natural transformations on the derived categories. Such naturality also holds for an inverted quasi-isomorphism: rearrange its naturality square by multiplying on both sides by its inverse. Hence it holds under all compositions after localization. Faithfulness of restriction in the tensor-descent statement now proves the two equations and the zero/addition laws globally. The same argument proves the unit identities from step 7 globally: view a transformation in $M$ alone as a bifunctor transformation independent of its second argument (and use the first-independent version for $N$). Faithfulness then tests it on representatives too. This proves the asserted naturality for every derived map, without using direct images or adjunctions of module functors.
